concepts.def: The challenge that the existence of an omnipotent, omnibenevolent God seems incompatible with the reality of evil and suffering in the world.
Moral evil results from free human choices, such as murder; natural evil arises from the world's workings, such as earthquakes and disease.
Mackie argued God and evil are logically incompatible (the inconsistent triad), while the evidential problem claims the amount of suffering makes God improbable.
Augustine saw evil as a privation of good, not a created thing, entering a perfect creation through the free fall of angels and humans.
Drawing on Irenaeus, Hick argued the world is a 'vale of soul-making' in which challenge and suffering enable free growth towards God.
The argument that genuine human freedom is so valuable that God is justified in permitting the possibility of evil that misused freedom brings.

Philosophy of Religion: Evil & Suffering — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of natural evil?
options: Suffering caused by an earthquake
Theft
Lying
A war crime

mcqs.q: For Augustine, evil is best described as what?
options: A privation of good rather than a substance God created
An equal and opposite force to God
A substance created by the devil
A useful illusion with no reality for anyone

mcqs.q: What does Hick's phrase 'vale of soul-making' claim?
options: A world containing challenge and suffering enables persons to grow freely towards God
The world was created perfect and remains so
Souls are repeatedly reincarnated until perfect
Evil conclusively proves there is no God

mcqs.q: Does the free will defence explain natural evil?
options: Its direct force concerns moral evil; to cover earthquakes and disease, defenders add further moves, such as Augustine's fallen world or Hick's claim that a law-governed, challenging world is needed for soul-making.
Free will straightforwardly explains why earthquakes and diseases occur.
The free will defence claims humans cause earthquakes by their choices.
A theodicy is a prayer asking God to remove evil.

mcqs.q: Is Augustine saying that evil and suffering are not real?
options: Augustine taught that God created evil as a separate substance.
No - privation means evil is a lack or corruption of good, as blindness is an absence of sight; the suffering is real, but evil has no independent created existence.
A theodicy is a prayer asking God to remove evil.
Augustine taught that evil is just an illusion that nobody really experiences.

mcqs.q: Does a theodicy claim that evil is secretly good?
options: The free will defence claims humans cause earthquakes by their choices.
No - a theodicy argues God has morally sufficient reasons for permitting genuinely bad things, such as preserving freedom or enabling growth; it does not deny evil's badness.
A theodicy is a prayer asking God to remove evil.
Theodicies say evil is really a good thing in disguise.
